targetText: The object of war, namely, the preservation of oneself and the destruction of the enemy, is the essence of war and the basis of all war activities, an essence which pervades all war activities, from the technical to the strategic.
summary: Every military tactic and strategy boils down to two interrelated goals: preserving one's own forces and destroying the enemy's capacity to resist.
explanation: Mao traces the dialectical unity of attack and defence from the ancient spear and shield to modern warfare: attack (destroying the enemy) is the primary means of self-preservation, while defence and partial sacrifice serve the preservation of the whole.
context: Whether a soldier takes cover while firing or a field army retreats to set up an ambush, both actions combine self-preservation with disarming the enemy.
